title: A lesson from three days ago is built into today's step
origin: Issue #77 (proof plus reflection): Should, a later step builds an earlier lesson in

history.text: [voice note] talked to the new guy on my team at lunch, it was fine but kinda died after 2 min
Two minutes with someone new is a real start, Sofia. We'll build on it tomorrow.

plan.step: Say hi and ask one coworker how their week is going at lunch
plan.destination: feel at ease making small talk at work
plan.proof_note: a quick voice note on how it went
plan.reason: One small conversation a day makes it feel normal.

step_days.step: Ask one coworker how their week is going at lunch
Ask one coworker a follow-up about their weekend
step_days.reflection: Asking a follow-up about what they just said kept it going way longer

step_days.step: Say hi to someone you haven't talked to yet
Lunch chat with the new guy on your team
step_days.reflection: It was fine but died after 2 minutes

takeaways.text: A follow-up about what they just said keeps a conversation going

whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: lessons should be put to use again a few days later.
shouldHaveHappened: The morning kickoff gives today's step fully defined (who or where, at lunch around 12:30, about how long) and builds in the follow-up lesson from three days ago, since yesterday's chat died after two minutes (for example: talk to the new guy again and ask a follow-up about whatever he says). It reads as coaching, not a quiz, and asks one thing (are they in). After "yeah ok I'm in" ZOH answers in a short line without restating the step.
